claims.text: Introducing a nanohierarchical architecture with composition undulation into CoCrFeNi will maintain a low coefficient of friction from room temperature to 800 °C.
Introducing a nanohierarchical architecture with composition undulation into CoCrFeNi will maintain a low wear rate from room temperature to 800 °C.
The nanohierarchical architecture with composition undulation provides a self-lubricating effect.
The nanohierarchical architecture with composition undulation reduces the contact area during sliding.
The nanohierarchical architecture with composition undulation increases surface hardness.
The combined self-lubricating effect, reduced contact area, and increased surface hardness decrease friction.
The combined self-lubricating effect, reduced contact area, and increased surface hardness decrease wear.
The modified CoCrFeNi alloy will have a lower coefficient of friction than CoCrFeNi without the nanohierarchical architecture.
The modified CoCrFeNi alloy will have a lower wear rate than CoCrFeNi without the nanohierarchical architecture.
The modified CoCrFeNi alloy will exhibit a wear rate on the order of 10^-7 to 10^-6 mm^3/Nm.
The proposed performance is expected to persist at loads up to 1000 N.
The proposed performance is expected to persist in environments with humidity up to 80%.
The interaction between the nanohierarchical architecture and the CoCrFeNi matrix is not fully understood.
